---
title: "Short session – the EU-frames case"
subtitle: "Two halves, with a facilitator"
---

This is the short session on the EU-frames case, for a slot of three hours, with nothing to install, no account to open and nothing preregistered. It works on a study of sixteen Eurobarometer waves, which asked whether the economic crisis changed how the citizens of the member states frame the European Union, and on a claim of the original author (OA) that five analysts reanalysed in the Multi100 project, with results from a partial correlation of −0.006 to one of −0.452. You write the estimand behind the claim, reproduce one of the recorded results, and then work as analyst number six: you take the analysis apart into its decisions, try alternatives one decision at a time, put the analysis that you would defend on the class chart, and read it against the curve of every defensible analysis of the claim.

You leave with an estimand statement, a reproduced result whose value you can explain, your own place among the 864 specifications of the curve, and a reading of what such a curve does and does not establish, next to a claim that was tested again on new data.

## How you work

The session runs entirely in the browser lab, a page of this site on which R runs inside your browser, with the data already in place. Open it in a tab of its own and keep this page beside it. Each half has a page that lists its steps in order, and every step at the keyboard has a button that opens the lab at the right task. The slides are on the [slides page](slides.qmd), and each half opens with a link to its place in the deck.

[Open the browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The deck exists in two versions. The plain deck is followed on the screen while the tasks run in the lab. The [live deck](../../live/eu-frames-short.html) carries the cells of the tasks on its own slides, with R loaded inside it, so that the facilitator and the class work inside one deck and the lab stays a fallback; it downloads the same files as the lab when it is opened.

The class writes its estimand statements, its reproduced values and its placements and sends them at the same moment, and the class chart draws the analysis of every participant, so the session needs a facilitator.

## The parts of the session

- **[Before the session](before.qmd)** (about an hour). You read the case study and open the browser lab once on the machine that you will bring.
- **[First half – The claim and its reproduction](half-1.qmd).** Three kinds of repetition and Multi100, the paper and its record, the estimand statement, and the reproduction of one of three recorded results.
- **[Second half – The multiverse of the claim](half-2.qmd).** The specification menu, your own tries and the class chart, the curve of 864 and how to read it, and the replication with new data.
- **[After the session](after.qmd).** Where to go next on this site.

[Start with Before the session](before.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

The same case is also taught as a [one-day workshop](../eu-frames-one-day/index.qmd), as the [Extended course](../eu-frames-extended/index.qmd), whose second day is the workshop, and as a [self-study route](../self-study/index.qmd).
